sentences.text:
This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER 1.

This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.46/2021 registered at Police Station Cyber Cell, Indore (M.P.) for the offence under Section 420, 419, 467, 468, 471 /34 of IPC and Section 66-C, 66-D, 74 of Information Technology Act.

2. As per the prosecution story, complainant Pawan Kumar Verma, Vice President of Pratibha Syntex Limited lodged a complaint against the present applicant and other co- accused persons by stating that their company namely ROSL/ROSCTL license worth Rs.1.25 Crores had been transferred to the 1 other company without the consent of their company.
Allegation levelled against the present applicant is that he has fraudulently obtained details of the said company and transferred the licence to the Black Curve Incorporation Company.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant contended that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this matter.
He is in custody since 22/0.5/2022.
Initially offence under Section 420/34 of IPC and Section 66-C, 66-D and 74 of the IT Act has been registered against him.
For the offence under Section 66-C and 66-D of IT Act, 3 years imprisonment is provided and for the offence under Section 74 of IT Act, two years imprisonment is provided.
Applicant is a permanent resident of District New Delhi.
Final conclusion of trial will take considerable long time.
Hence, he prays that applicant be released on bail.

4. Per-contra, learned PL for respondent/State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that two more criminal antecedents of similar nature have been found against the present applicant.
He is a habitual offender and the amount in question is more than Rs.27 Crores.

5. Counsel for the objector also opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that the applicant after getting information of the Directors of the company from the website of ROC and taking print of the documents, prepared forged DSC of the Directors of the complainant company Pratibha Syntex and prepared forged Adhar Card and PAN Card of the Directors of the company.
There is sufficient prima facie evidence available against the applicant, therefore, he does not deserve for bail.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary as well as status report sent by the trial Court.
7.
As per the status report, charges have been framed and the case is fixed for prosecution evidence.

8. From perusal of the case diary and the documents available on record, it appears that prima facie sufficient evidence is available against the present applicant and he has taken active participation in the aforesaid offence by preparing the fake DSC certificate and illegally transferring 10 licences of the complainant company to the Black Curve company.
Forged DSC, Adhar Card, PAN card and other documents were prepared by the applicant.

Bail application of co-accused Manish has already been dismissed on merit by this Court vide order dated 12/12/2023 passed in MCRC no.
28984/2023 in similar circumstances.
The matter pertains to cheating and forgery of more than Rs.27 Crores.

The applicant is having criminal antecedents of similar nature.
9.
In view of the prima facie evidence available on record, this Court is not inclined to grant regular bail to the applicant.
Hence, this second bail application is dismissed.
